judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long delivery provision with nested provisos (x), (y) and (z); the phrase 'or such later date as is agreed to' leaves the Mortgage File Delivery Date open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to Exhibit 6 for lost notes (which merely says 'Available Upon Request') and to Section 6(a) for the recording carve-out, and Section 6(a) is itself garbled, so the 180-day recording duty is hard to pin down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says 'EMC or MSMCH, as applicable ... will cause, at EMC's own expense', putting the cost on EMC even when MSMCH is the responsible Seller.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also purports to bind the Master Servicer ('the Master Servicer agrees that it will not'), who is not a party to this Agreement at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad access language ('from time to time', 'such due diligence as any such party reasonably believes is appropriate') but each phrase is a familiar reasonableness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves rights to 'demand cure, repurchase, substitution or other relief', which sits uneasily with Section 10's declaration that cure/purchase/substitution is the sole and exclusive remedy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear mechanics for reassignment on repurchase or substitution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes affirmative duties on the Trustee, who is not a signatory here, and it presupposes substitution requirements that Section 10 and the Replacement Mortgage Loan definition never supply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is plainly defective: a clause breaks off at 'at no expense to' and jumps into an unnumbered list, and two separate items are both numbered '(iv)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It declares a failure to record to be 'a Material Defect' and directs that 'the provisions of Section 5(c) and (d) shall apply' when Section 5 has only subsections (a) and (b), and Material Defect is nowhere defined.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard true-sale/back-up security interest clause, though it cites 'Section 9-305 (or comparable provision)' of the UCC, a section superseded by the time of drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly reconciles itself with Section 4 and the Pooling and Servicing Agreement; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory sentence; 'as to itself in the capacity indicated' is filler.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel intros in Sections 9 and 13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional organization and standing representation with a materiality qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 28's covenant to maintain existence and qualification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line power representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 9(b) and 13(b); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict language; 'the provisions hereof or thereof' refers to a 'thereof' with no antecedent, since only one agreement is mentioned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Sections 9(c) and 13(c); no operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-consents representation with an express carve-out for pending recordations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recording obligations in Sections 4(b) and 6(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability language with the usual bankruptcy qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 9(e) and 13(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains a dropped verb — 'and EMC not in default with respect to any order' — so the final clause is ungrammatical as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel MSMCH representation in Section 9(f) reads 'MSMCH is not in default', confirming the omission is a slip rather than a different meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines its own subject by cross-reference — 'the Mortgage Loan Seller's Information (as defined in Section 14(a) hereof)' — to a definition that does not exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14(a) is the Conditions to Closing provision and contains no such definition, so this disclosure representation has no ascertainable subject matter anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence 'has full right and authority to subject to no interest or participation of, or agreement with, any other party' is garbled, and the whole of EMC's loan-level warranty is a single ownership representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10's cure/purchase/substitution machinery and the sole-remedy clause address only Section 10 breaches, so a breach of this Section 8 representation has no stated remedy; Section 19 compounds this by citing 'Sections 5 and 7'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Sections 7 and 13; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional organization and standing representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 28's covenant for MSMCH.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line power representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 7(b) and 13(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard no-conflict language, again with an orphan 'or thereof'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 7(c); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-consents representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 7(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 7(e) and 13(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-litigation representation, complete as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Sections 7(f) and 13(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as of the Closing Date or such other date as may be specified below' leaves the reference date floating, but that is a common formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs to the Purchaser only, while Sections 7 and 9 also run to the other Seller, and subsection (b) narrows the reps to MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'complete, true and correct' is a firm absolute standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made 'with respect to each Mortgage Loan', i.e. including EMC's loans, although MSMCH is the only maker of Section 10 representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of statutes followed by an open catch-all ('any federal, state or local law including, without limitation'), the classic general-versus-specific setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Exhibit F Part B(C) of the Underlying Agreement and overlaps Section 10(a)(3); overlap but no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No Mortgage Loan is a High Cost Loan or Covered Loan, as applicable' — the qualifier 'as applicable' has no evident work to do and blurs the absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the HOEPA prong already inside the High Cost Loan definition, making the second sentence redundant rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delinquency is measured by a defined term ('Delinquent') that this Agreement does not itself define, and the carve-out 'other than payments not yet 30 days Delinquent' is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Delinquent' must be imported from the Pooling and Servicing Agreement under Section 1; the Underlying Agreement defines it differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-defenses warranty, absolute in terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical in substance to Exhibit F Part A(B); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a generally acceptable insurer' and hazards 'customarily insured against in the jurisdiction' are standards without fixed boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(C) of the Underlying Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted-encumbrance list ends with a catch-all — '(iv) other matters to which like properties are commonly subject which do not materially interfere' — set against three specific items.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(b)(6) cross-refers to clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) of this paragraph, and that cross-reference is accurate here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'have been duly and properly executed by other such related parties' should read 'such other', a slip that changes who is warranted to have executed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit F Part A(F) contains the identical wording, so the error is carried through rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense title-insurance warranty that turns on 'Co-op Loan', a term never defined in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cross-reference to clauses (i)-(iii) of paragraph (4) is accurate, but 'Co-op Loan' has to be borrowed from the Underlying Agreement or the Pooling and Servicing Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-defaults warranty with an accurate internal cross-reference to paragraph (1).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 10(b)(1); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A full-disbursement warranty, specific and absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(I).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-mechanics-liens warranty; the parenthetical about inchoate rights is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(J).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'customary and enforceable provisions such as to render the rights and remedies ... adequate' is a standard with no ascertainable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(K); no internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A due-on-sale warranty, doubly hedged ('enforceable provision ... and to the best of MSMCH's knowledge, such provision is enforceable').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(L).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each Mortgaged Property is in good repair' is an unqualified vague standard sitting next to a knowledge-qualified condemnation statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'taking into such facts as, without limitation' is ungrammatical, and the whole representation about what a borrower 'may have qualified for' is inherently indeterminate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single word, '[Reserved]'; nothing to construe.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(P).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'if necessary to protect the interests of the Purchaser' and 'to the extent required' are soft qualifiers on an otherwise absolute no-modification warranty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires delivery to the Trustee, consistent with Section 4(b), and matches Exhibit F Part A(Q).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tax-status warranty keyed to a specific Code section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(R).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in 'Solely with respect to the Fremont Mortgage Loans, the New Century Mortgage Loans and any First NLC ... and Accredited Mortgage Loans sold by MSMCH' is a narrow carve-in inside a subsection expressed to cover a different set of loans.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fremont and Accredited are not within the defined MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans that subsection (b) governs, so this warranty either expands that defined set or is a nullity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An encroachment and zoning warranty, absolute and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(T).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses 'Qualified Appraiser' as a defined term and then restates the definition, and this Agreement does not define it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Qualified Appraiser' is defined in the Underlying Agreement by reference to FIRREA only, while this clause adds Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'LTV' is used as an abbreviation that this Agreement never defines, and the definitions section instead defines 'Value' and refers to Loan-to-Value Ratio.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Mortgage Loan Schedule definition speaks of Loan-to-Value Ratio and CLTV, so which ratio the 100% cap tests is not settled by the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layered warranty with different limits for pre- and post-October 2002 loans and a modification proviso; workable but dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Exhibit F Part A(W), which Subsection 8.02 deems automatically material.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three parallel absolute statements about single-premium credit insurance; the 'e.g.' lists are illustrative but the prohibition is clear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated, absolute no-arbitration warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear survival language, though the second sentence shifts to 'the related Mortgage Loan Seller' after a section made only by MSMCH.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That shift matters because EMC makes no Section 10 representations, so deeming 'the related Mortgage Loan Seller' to repeat them on substitution does not fit Sections 8 and 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the classic contested formula: 'materially and adversely affects the value of the interests of the Purchaser', 'prompt written notice', a 90-day window measured from discovery or notice 'whichever occurs earlier', and an election among cure, purchase or substitution declared to be the 'sole and exclusive remedy'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 5(a)'s preservation of 'other relief', Section 19's statement that the Trustee's sole remedy is 'contained in Sections 5 and 7', and the accrual paragraph that follows; the remedy architecture does not line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'a breach of a representation or warranty set forth in this Section 10 made by Accredited', but Accredited makes no representation anywhere in Section 10, so the trigger for the backstop is unstated on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10(b) is limited to MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, which exclude Accredited loans, and the cure period is borrowed from the AAR Agreement attached as Exhibit 8, which the text does not reproduce; the backstop cannot be reconciled with Section 10's own scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An accrual clause purporting to defer when a cause of action arises until both discovery/notice and a failure to cure, which is precisely the kind of language litigated over limitations periods.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the 90-day cure paragraph and with the parallel accrual sentence in Underlying Agreement Subsection 8.02, and it does not address the Accredited backstop timing at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section merely assigns two agreements; the heading in the body differs from the table of contents heading, and 'BSABS I' is used without definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2(a), 2(c) and 20 all treat Section 11 as containing the conditions to closing, which it plainly does not; that misdirection runs through the payment and termination provisions.
